title: A torn shirt told the truth when words could not.
subtitle: How the evidence cleared Yusuf
then: The wife of the 'Aziz accused Yusuf at the door. A witness from her own household said: look at how the shirt is torn. Ibn Kathir explains that when her husband saw it {idea}torn from the back{/idea}, he was certain Yusuf had run and she had pursued. He said: {trap}this is a plot of you women.{/trap}
now: Someone tells the manager a story about you before you even walk in. The group chat has already decided. You feel you have to shout to be heard. {idea}Sometimes the quiet facts speak better than you can.{/idea} Truth often leaves a mark.
old: Whoever tells the story first gets believed.
new: Allah can bring the truth out through the smallest detail, even a torn shirt.
try: Next time you are falsely blamed, state the facts once, calmly, and leave the rest to Allah.

title: Keep it quiet, he said, and ask forgiveness.
subtitle: The husband covers the scandal instead of fixing it
then: The 'Aziz now knew the truth. Ibn Kathir says he told Yusuf to {trap}keep silent about what happened{/trap} and told his wife to ask forgiveness for her sin. He was an easy-going man, and he excused her. The family name was protected, but Yusuf was still in the house with the woman who had lied about him.
now: A relative crosses a line at a family gathering. Everyone agrees: let's not talk about it. The one who was wronged is told to just move on. {idea}Silence can protect a reputation and still leave a person unprotected.{/idea}
old: If we keep it quiet, the problem goes away.
new: Covering a wrong is not the same as making it right for the one who was hurt.
try: Think of one situation you hushed up. Ask yourself if someone is still paying for it.

title: The city's women judged her, and gossip spread fast.
subtitle: When a private sin becomes public talk
then: The 'Aziz had asked for silence, but the story spread through the city. Women of the chiefs and princes criticized his wife. Ibn Kathir quotes Muhammad bin Ishaq: {trap}they had heard of Yusuf's beauty and said these words to get a look at him.{/trap} The verse calls their talk scheming, not concern.
now: The voice note forwarded with a sigh: so sad, can you believe it? The comments under someone's bad moment. {trap}Gossip often dresses up as disapproval.{/trap} {idea}Ask what you really want when you pass it on.{/idea}
old: I am only saying what everyone already knows.
new: Talking about someone's fall can be its own hidden appetite.
try: The next piece of gossip that reaches you today, let it stop with you.

title: One look, and the critics cut their own hands.
subtitle: The banquet that silenced the gossips
then: Hearing their talk, the 'Aziz's wife invited them, gave each {trap}a knife and fruit to cut{/trap}, and called Yusuf out. Ibn Kathir says they were so stunned they cut their hands without noticing. They cried: {idea}Perfect is Allah, this is no human, only a noble angel.{/idea} He was given, as an authentic hadith says, half of all beauty.
now: You judge a friend for being swept away by something: a job offer, a person, a habit. Then you meet the same pull and lose your footing in a minute. {idea}It is easy to be firm about a test you have not faced.{/idea}
old: I would never fall for that.
new: The ones quickest to blame were overwhelmed the moment they faced the same thing.
try: Think of someone you judged harshly. Make one quiet dua for them instead.

title: She admitted he refused, then threatened him with prison.
subtitle: A confession and a threat in one breath

row.title: now you see
sub: this is the one you blamed me for

then: In front of the women, the 'Aziz's wife confessed: {idea}I sought to seduce him, but he firmly refused.{/idea} Some scholars said she was telling them about his inner beauty too, chaste inside and out. Then she threatened him openly: {trap}if he does not obey, he will be imprisoned and humiliated.{/trap}
now: Your boss hints that your contract depends on signing off on something wrong. A friend group says you are out unless you join in. {trap}Pressure often comes with a price tag attached to saying no.{/trap} {idea}The no itself is the proof of who you are.{/idea}
old: If refusing costs me this much, maybe I should give in.
new: A threat for refusing is a sign the refusal was right.
try: Name one pressure you are under right now and write down what saying no would protect.

title: Prison is dearer to me than what they call me to.
subtitle: Yusuf chooses the cell and asks for help

row.title: do not leave me to myself

then: Yusuf was young, and the one calling him had beauty, wealth and rank. Ibn Kathir says he {reward}preferred prison{/reward} because he feared Allah. His prayer meant: {idea}if You leave me to rely on myself, I have no power over myself.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ named among the seven shaded on the Day a man invited by such a woman who says, I fear Allah.
now: The late-night message you know you should not answer. The shortcut at work everyone takes. You think: I can handle it. {idea}Yusuf did not trust his strength. He asked Allah not to leave him alone with it.{/idea}
old: I can resist this on my own if I try hard enough.
new: Even the strongest say: Lord, if You leave me to myself, I will fall.
try: Before a moment you know tempts you, say Yusuf's words: Lord, turn it away from me.

title: He asked, and his Lord answered and turned it away.
subtitle: A prayer for protection, heard at once
then: Right after Yusuf's prayer, the verse says {reward}his Lord responded{/reward} and turned their plot away from him. Ibn Kathir says Allah protected him from error and saved him from giving in. The verse ends with two names: {idea}the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.{/idea}
now: You whispered a prayer in the car park before a hard meeting. You asked for help with a habit at 2 a.m. and it felt like nobody heard. {idea}The One who answered Yusuf hears that whisper and knows exactly what you are up against.{/idea}
old: My small private prayers probably do not reach anywhere.
new: A prayer for protection is heard, and the answer can come straight away.
try: Ask Allah today, in your own words, to protect you from one specific weakness.

title: They knew he was innocent and jailed him anyway.
subtitle: Prison to save face
then: Even after they saw {idea}the proofs of his innocence{/idea}, they decided to imprison Yusuf. Ibn Kathir suggests they wanted people to think {trap}Yusuf was the guilty one{/trap}, since the news had spread. Years later he would refuse to leave prison until his name was cleared.
now: The intern blamed so the senior manager keeps his bonus. The child punished because the adult is embarrassed. {trap}Sometimes people know the truth and still choose their image.{/trap} {idea}Allah sees the full file.{/idea}
old: If I am treated unfairly, it must mean my truth did not count.
new: People can bury the truth for a time, but they cannot erase it.
try: If you have let someone else carry blame that was yours, take one step to set it right.

title: Even in prison, people saw goodness in him.
subtitle: Two cellmates bring their dreams to Yusuf
then: Two young men entered the prison with Yusuf. Qatadah said one was {idea}the king's wine-server{/idea} and the other his baker. Each had a dream. They came to Yusuf because, they said, {reward}we see you are one of those who do good.{/reward}
now: You are stuck in a job you did not choose, a hospital ward, a hard season. You think it is wasted time. {idea}People still notice how you treat them there.{/idea} The way you behave in a low place can open the next door.
old: In a place like this, how I act does not matter.
new: Good character shows most clearly in the worst rooms, and people see it.
try: Wherever you feel stuck today, do one kind thing for someone stuck with you.

title: Before the dreams, he told them who taught him.
subtitle: Yusuf uses their trust to point to Allah

row.title: left a way
sub: that denies Allah and the Hereafter

then: Yusuf told the two men he would explain their dreams {idea}before their next food arrived{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says he first made clear that {reward}this knowledge was from Allah{/reward}, given because he left the way of people who did not believe in Allah or the Last Day. He called them to Tawhid before interpreting.
now: Someone praises your work in the meeting. Your exam result. The client who says you are a genius. {idea}You can take the compliment and still name where the skill came from.{/idea} Yusuf turned attention from himself to his Lord.
old: My talent is mine, I earned it.
new: Every skill I have was taught to me by my Lord.
try: When someone praises you today, quietly say alhamdulillah and mean it.

title: I follow my fathers Ibrahim, Ishaq and Yaqub.
subtitle: Belief in One God as a favor, not a burden

row.title: a favor
sub: on us and on all people

then: Yusuf told his cellmates he followed the way of {idea}Ibrahim, Ishaq and Yaqub{/idea} and would never set up partners with Allah. Ibn Kathir explains that this belief is {reward}a grace from Allah to us and to mankind{/reward}, sent through the Messengers. Yet most people do not thank Him for it, as in 14:28.
now: Your grandmother's prayer mat. The way your father said bismillah before driving. You may think of faith as something handed to you, heavy. {reward}It is the best inheritance you were given.{/reward}
old: Religion is a list of things I have to carry.
new: Knowing Allah is a gift passed down to me, and most people forget to thank Him for it.
try: Thank Allah today, by name, for one person who taught you about Him.

title: Many scattered masters, or the One who prevails?
subtitle: A simple question asked in a prison cell
then: Yusuf kept calling his two prison companions. Their people worshipped idols. He asked them plainly: {trap}are many separate lords better{/trap}, or {idea}Allah, the One, the Irresistible{/idea}? Ibn Kathir says everything has submitted to His kingdom.
now: Your boss's approval. Your followers' likes. Your in-laws' opinion. Your bank balance. {trap}Each one is a small master with its own demands.{/trap} {idea}One Lord means one set of expectations to live for.{/idea}
old: I have to keep everyone happy at once.
new: Serving One Master is freedom from serving many.
try: Name one opinion you are living for. Today, do one thing purely for Allah instead.

title: Only names you and your fathers made up.
subtitle: Inherited habits with no proof behind them
then: Yusuf told the men their idols were {trap}only names forged and handed from one generation to the next{/trap}, with no proof from Allah. Ibn Kathir says he affirmed that {idea}judgement and command belong to Allah alone{/idea}, and that this is the straight religion, though most people do not know. Then he turned to their dreams.
now: The family custom nobody questions. The thing everyone at work does because it has always been done. {trap}Habit is not the same as proof.{/trap} {idea}Ask where a rule came from before you give your life to it.{/idea}
old: If my family has always done it, it must be right.
new: A tradition needs a source from Allah, not just a long history.
try: Pick one habit you follow without thinking and ask honestly: who said this?
